prompt: A teammate quietly helps everyone with their problems and rarely asks for anything herself.
why: Supportive, patient and modest is S.
trap: An i is helpful too, but more visibly and socially.

prompt: When the team announces a new tool next week, one colleague asks, 'Why change? The old one works fine.'
tells: 'Why change? The old one works fine.'
why: S values stability and needs time to adjust to change.
trap: C might resist too, but would ask for evidence the new tool is better.

prompt: In a tense meeting, she agrees with everyone and later tells a friend she actually disagreed.
tells: later tells a friend she actually disagreed
why: S avoids open conflict to keep harmony.
trap: C would state the disagreement, with reasons.

prompt: Asked for a decision on the spot, he says 'Can I think about it and get back to you tomorrow?'
why: S prefers time to consider, especially how changes affect people.
trap: C also wants time, but to analyze data, and would usually ask for it.

prompt: She has been on the same team for nine years and is the one who remembers everyone's birthday.
why: Loyalty and care for the team are S.
trap: An i remembers people too, but is drawn to new people and excitement.

prompt: Under pressure, a normally easygoing teammate goes quiet, says yes to everything, and quietly falls behind.
why: Under stress, S becomes passive and has trouble saying no.
trap: C under stress withdraws into detail and becomes critical.

prompt: He likes knowing exactly how each week will go and gets uneasy when the schedule changes at the last minute.
tells: gets uneasy when the schedule changes
trap: C likes structure too, but for accuracy, not comfort.

prompt: When two colleagues argue, she's the one who calms things down and finds something both can agree on.
why: Seeking harmony and smoothing conflict is S.
trap: An i might lighten the mood with humor, but S works to restore calm.

prompt: He looks uncomfortable when praised at the all-hands, but treasures a handwritten note from his manager.
trap: An i would love the all-hands moment.

prompt: Her first question about any reorganization is 'How will this affect the people on my team?'
tells: How will this affect the people on my team?
why: Concern for people and stability is S.
trap: D's first question would be about results.
